# Review pack: Ismail

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/ismail.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This subject is mentioned briefly or beside others, so the draft is short and states only what the cited ayat state. The chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about this prophet. None is used in this draft.
- The inventory does not include the passage on the vision of a sacrifice (37:99-113), and this draft does not use it. That passage does not name the son, and this draft does not decide who he is; a scholar should say how the page should treat the question.
- 2:127-128: the prayer has no verb of speech and no named speaker; the draft states only the plural wording and the dual 'both', and leaves the speakers open. A scholar should check the wording.
- 2:127: the draft says Ismail is named beside Ibrahim and does not say that he raised the foundations; a scholar should decide whether the Arabic supports saying more.
- 14:39: the speaker is not named in that verse; the draft reads it as Ibrahim because it sits in the prayer opened by his name. The verses 14:36-38 and 14:40-41 are not used.
- 19:55: the Arabic word that can mean household or people is rendered 'household'.
- The prayers at 2:126 and 2:129 and the rest of 14:35-41 are Ibrahim's prayers that do not name Ismail and are not used.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later writers gave Ismail a place of residence, a mother, a lifespan and a role in the house; none of this is used.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Beside Ibrahim  (`#beside-ibrahim`)

Cited ayat: 2:125, 2:127-128, 14:35, 14:39

> **2:125** وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا ٱلْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا وَٱتَّخِذُوا۟ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمَ مُصَلًّى وَعَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْعَٰكِفِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ

> **2:127** وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّآ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
>
> **2:128** رَبَّنَا وَٱجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةً مُّسْلِمَةً لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَآ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

> **14:35** وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدَ ءَامِنًا وَٱجْنُبْنِى وَبَنِىَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ

> **14:39** ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى وَهَبَ لِى عَلَى ٱلْكِبَرِ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ إِنَّ رَبِّى لَسَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ

### Claims

**c1** (2:125): God made the house a place of return and of safety for people, and a place where Ibrahim stood is to be taken as a place of prayer.

**c2** (2:125): God made a covenant with Ibrahim and Ismail: they were to purify His house for those who go around it, those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate.

**c3** (2:127): Ibrahim raised the foundations of the house, and Ismail is named in the same verse beside him.

**c4** (2:127): A prayer follows in the first person plural, asking the Lord to accept from the speakers, and calling Him the One who hears and knows.

**c5** (2:128): The prayer goes on to ask that both speakers be made submissive to Him, that a community submissive to Him come from their offspring, that He show them their rites of worship, and that He turn to them; it calls Him the One who accepts repentance, the Merciful.

**c6** (14:35): In a prayer, Ibrahim asked his Lord to make this land secure and to keep him and his sons away from worshipping idols.

**c7** (14:39): Later in the same prayer, the speaker praises God, who gave him Ismail and Ishaq in his old age, and says that his Lord hears prayer.

### One-minute summary

God made a covenant with Ibrahim and Ismail to purify His house for those who go around it, stay in it and pray [c2]. Ibrahim raised the foundations of the house, with Ismail named beside him, and a prayer follows [c3][c4]. In another prayer, the speaker praises God for giving him Ismail and Ishaq in his old age [c7].

### Complete story

God made the house a place of return and of safety for people [c1]. A place where Ibrahim stood is to be taken as a place of prayer [c1].

God made a covenant with Ibrahim and Ismail: they were to purify His house for those who go around it, those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate [c2]. Ibrahim raised the foundations of the house, and Ismail is named in the same verse beside him [c3]. A prayer follows in the first person plural, asking the Lord to accept from the speakers [c4]. It goes on to ask that both speakers be made submissive to Him, that a community submissive to Him come from their offspring, that He show them their rites of worship, and that He turn to them [c5].

In another prayer, Ibrahim asked his Lord to make this land secure and to keep him and his sons away from worshipping idols [c6]. Later in the same prayer, the speaker praises God, who gave him Ismail and Ishaq in his old age, and says that his Lord hears prayer [c7].

### Deep study

The covenant names both men as the ones charged with purifying the house, and names the people the house is for: those who go around it, those who stay, those who bow and prostrate [c2]. The verse on the foundations names Ibrahim as the one who raises them and Ismail beside him [c3]. The prayer that follows speaks of 'us' and, in the next verse, of both speakers together [c4][c5]. The verse that names Ismail and Ishaq as a gift does not name its speaker; it sits inside the prayer that Ibrahim begins, and the gift is given in old age [c6][c7].

### Kids mode

God asked Ibrahim and Ismail to keep His house pure for the people who come to go around it and to pray [c2]. Ibrahim raised the foundations of the house and Ismail was named beside him [c3]. A prayer followed, asking God to accept their work [c4]. In another prayer, the speaker thanked God for giving him Ismail and Ishaq when he was old [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the covenant shows a task shared by a pair, since both are named in it [c2]. Another is that the work is followed by a prayer for acceptance, so that building is joined to turning to God [c4][c5]. A further reading is that thanks for a gift can sit in the same prayer as a request to be kept from idol worship [c6][c7].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the verses do not name the place where the house stood, its size, how long the work took, or how old Ismail was.
- Not established: who speaks the prayer after the foundations. The text gives a plural 'us' and a form for both speakers, and does not name them.
- Not established: whether Ismail took part in the raising of the foundations or is named beside Ibrahim for another reason; the wording names him right after Ibrahim and says no more.
- Not established: what 'purify' covers in the covenant.
- Not established: the age of Ibrahim, Ismail or Ishaq, or how far apart the sons were born.
- Not established: which land the other prayer means by 'this land'. The verses of that prayer between the ones used here are not told in this chapter.

## 2. True to his promise  (`#true-to-his-promise`)

Cited ayat: 19:54-55

> **19:54** وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صَادِقَ ٱلْوَعْدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَّبِيًّا
>
> **19:55** وَكَانَ يَأْمُرُ أَهْلَهُۥ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ وَكَانَ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ مَرْضِيًّا

### Claims

**c1** (19:54): Ismail is named for remembrance and is described as true to his promise, and as a messenger and a prophet.

**c2** (19:55): He used to tell his household to pray and to give zakat, and he was one with whom his Lord was pleased.

### One-minute summary

Ismail is described as true to his promise, a messenger and a prophet [c1]. He told his household to pray and give zakat, and his Lord was pleased with him [c2].

### Complete story

Ismail is named for remembrance and is described as true to his promise, and as a messenger and a prophet [c1]. He used to tell his household to pray and to give zakat, and he was one with whom his Lord was pleased [c2].

### Deep study

Ismail is described as true to his promise, as a messenger and as a prophet [c1]. The verse after it adds his instruction to his household and his Lord's pleasure with him [c2].

### Kids mode

Ismail kept his promises [c1]. He told his family to pray and to give zakat, and God was pleased with him [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the verses place keeping a promise beside caring for one's own household in prayer [c1][c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which promise is meant, or to whom it was made.
- Not established: whether the Arabic word for his household means his family or his people; this draft keeps 'household'.
- Not established: where Ismail lived, to whom he was sent, or what his message was.

## 3. Among the patient and the best  (`#among-the-patient-and-the-best`)

Cited ayat: 21:85-86, 38:48

> **21:85** وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
>
> **21:86** وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

> **38:48** وَٱذْكُرْ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلْيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلْأَخْيَارِ

### Claims

**c1** (21:85): Ismail is named together with Idris and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the patient.

**c2** (21:86): God says that He admitted them into His mercy, and that they were among the righteous.

**c3** (38:48): Ismail is named again, with Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the best.

### One-minute summary

Ismail is named with Idris and Dhul-Kifl as one of the patient [c1]. God admitted them into His mercy and called them righteous [c2]. In another passage Ismail is named with Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl as one of the best [c3].

### Complete story

Ismail is named together with Idris and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the patient [c1]. God says that He admitted them into His mercy, and that they were among the righteous [c2].

Ismail is named again, with Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the best [c3].

### Deep study

The passages group Ismail with different companions: Idris and Dhul-Kifl in one [c1], Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl in the other [c3]. The passage with Idris adds that God admitted them to His mercy and that they were righteous [c2].

### Kids mode

God named Ismail with Idris and Dhul-Kifl and said each of them was patient [c1]. God took them into His mercy [c2]. In another place God named Ismail with Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl and said each was among the best [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that patience is the quality singled out in the passage with Idris and that mercy is joined to it [c1][c2]. The passage with Alyasa names a different quality, being among the best [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what Ismail was patient in, or when or where.
- Not established: the sense in which the passage with Alyasa calls them 'the best'; the verse gives the word and no example.
- Not established: whether the lists describe one gathering or separate ones.
